subject: Availability & p95 latency evidence — procurement follow-up
messages:
From: Samir Kahn <samir.kahn@remorahealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@remorahealth.com
Date: Thu, 9 Oct 2025 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Availability & p95 latency evidence — procurement follow-up

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — Remora's procurement team asked me to pull together a short list of artifacts they need to complete our security & procurement checklist. We're specifically focused on the availability and latency commitments called out in the draft MSA (uptime % and p95 latency targets).

Can you confirm:
- How uptime is measured (what metric, what aggregation window, what monitoring tier)?
- How p95 and p99 latency are computed (end-to-end or host-level; rolling window)?
- What monitoring tooling you use (do you expose Grafana dashboards or only periodic extracts)?
- Whether you can provide short-term dashboard access (read-only) for audit reviewers, or if we need a packaged evidence bundle instead.

Procurement would also like a single zipped evidence packet with the last 90 days of aggregated SLO graphs and any incident runbook excerpts that show remediation timelines. If you can attach a suggested procurement questionnaire response, that would speed things up.

Thanks — if easier, loop in whoever owns instrumentation.

—Samir
Head of IT, Remora Health

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samir Kahn <samir.kahn@remorahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Oct 2025 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Availability & p95 latency evidence — procurement follow-up

Hi Samir — great question, and happy to provide everything procurement needs. High level answers below; I attached a compact evidence packet and a draft questionnaire response for your reviewers. If they'd prefer live access, we can provide a time-limited, read-only Grafana/Grafana-backed Redwood Console invite (typical window is 14–30 days).

Summary (short):
- Uptime: measured as rolling 30-day availability for the inference control plane and model-serving pool. We calculate successful request ratio (2xx responses / total requests) sampled at 1-minute resolution and aggregated to 95/99 percentiles over the rolling window. We also maintain a 12-month availability ledger for contractual reporting.
- p95/p99 latency: reported as end-to-end server-side token-generation latency (time between request accepted by our edge and final token returned), computed on completed calls only. We compute p50/p90/p95/p99 over configurable windows (1h, 24h, 30d). By default contract metrics use 30-day windows unless otherwise negotiated.
- Instrumentation & tools: primary telemetry is Prometheus for metrics ingestion, with Grafana and our Redwood Console overlay for dashboards and traces. We also export aggregated latency histograms and percentile calculations to the Console; raw traces live in New Relic for debugging.
- Dashboard access: we offer read-only dashboard invites scoped to a single account and limited by time and view (no K/V cache dumps or raw traces by default). For compliance reviewers we can apply a temporary broadened view for up to 30 days under an NDA and with audit logging of viewer accounts.

I've attached:
- procurement-questionnaire-Remora.pdf (draft responses)
- slo-evidence-packet.zip (graphs: 30d and 90d p95/p99, uptime ledger, incident summaries)
- dashboard-screenshot-20251008.png (sample Console view)

If procurement needs the raw export (CSV/histogram buckets) we typically require a data-sharing addendum; otherwise the aggregated graphs are sufficient in 95% of audits.

Next steps: if procurement can point to the exact fields they need on the questionnaire, I can get Marissa (SRE liaison) to prepare a limited-read Console invite for your audit team.

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
T: +1 415 555 0132

Subject: Re: Availability & p95 latency evidence — procurement follow-up

On behalf of procurement — thank you for the packet. A couple of clarifications before we ask audit to use a Console invite:

1) For the p95 number: do you compute this using a rolling 30-day window aligned to calendar days, or a sliding window anchored to each event? We need to know for our scoring.
2) Can you provide a sample CSV of the percentile buckets for the last 14 days (not raw traces, just the histogram buckets and aggregated p50/p95/p99)?
3) For uptime ledger: we need an explicit definition of "successful request" (does it include 3xx redirects; what about canceled client connections?) and the incident timeline extract for any availability incident that impacted >0.5% of traffic in the last 12 months.

If you can provide the short CSV and the success-definition line, procurement will sign off and send this to legal for the final MSA redline. We can proceed with a read-only invite if you attach an NDA template or confirm the existing procurement NDA covers viewer access.

—Procurement Team (Remora Health)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: procurement@remorahealth.com, Samir Kahn <samir.kahn@remorahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Oct 2025 12:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Availability & p95 latency evidence — procurement follow-up

Thanks — quick answers below and next steps. Quoting your questions for clarity:

> 1) For the p95 number: do you compute this using a rolling 30-day window aligned to calendar days, or a sliding window anchored to each event?

We compute percentiles using a sliding (continuous) window aggregated at 1-minute resolution and then bucketted into hourly/24h/30d rollups for reporting. For contractual metrics we publish the 30-day rolling number aligned to UTC calendar days by default (this avoids surprises for billing/reporting). If you need sliding-window clauses in the contract we can add that language — most customers prefer the 30-day UTC window for consistency.

> 2) Can you provide a sample CSV of the percentile buckets for the last 14 days (not raw traces, just the histogram buckets and aggregated p50/p95/p99)?

Yes — attached inside slo-evidence-packet.zip is a sample CSV (./exports/14d_latency_buckets.csv). If you need a different bucketization, Marissa can regenerate.

> 3) For uptime ledger: we need an explicit definition of "successful request" (does it include 3xx redirects; what about canceled client connections?)

Definition: a successful request is a server-acknowledged request resulting in a final 2xx HTTP status (generation success). 3xx responses are counted as non-success for the purposes of the uptime metric unless specifically configured by the customer. Canceled client connections (client closed before final token) are excluded from the denominator if the server never returned a final HTTP response; otherwise they count depending on final status code. We'll include this exact text in the procurement questionnaire response.

Incident extract: inside the ZIP there is an incidents.md file with all incidents that impacted >0.5% traffic in the last 12 months including start/end, impact estimate, root cause, and remediation steps.

NDA: we can either accept Remora's standard procurement NDA or sign a Redwood viewer-specific addendum for the Console invite. I'll loop Marissa and Ben to get a short-read invite created and to confirm the CSV extract format.

Action items:
- Marissa: prepare 14d CSV sample and confirm bucket boundaries (we used 0-50ms/50-100/100-200/200-500/500-1000/1000+ for the sample).
- Ben: prepare the limited read-only Console invite template and attach audit logging defaults.
- Jordan: upload the finalized questionnaire PDF to the HubSpot deal and send the invite link once NDA is sorted.

I'll follow up separately with the HubSpot link and the invite URL.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
